candidates.title: Prepare a restaurant order alert

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare a notification when a new restaurant website order arrives.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to build an automated restaurant order notification system using Make.com .

ease.reason: A beginner can test formatting operator-supplied sample orders, but the source documents no trigger or message delivery capability.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small restaurants may pay for order alerts; this request establishes neither buyer intent nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can turn synthetic order details into alert drafts; website access and live delivery remain unsupported.

autonomy.reason: A proposed formatter can prepare alerts, but no evidence supports automatic triggering or delivery and a person must verify them.

evidence.reason: The request names an automated restaurant order-notification system, but gives no frequency, setup details, or payment evidence.

candidates.reason: A synthetic-order alert experiment is concrete, but unsupported trigger and delivery mechanics keep the assessment below threshold.

candidates.title: Draft customer status updates from changing data

demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I’d be interested to hear how others handle customer-facing status updates when internal operational data is incomplete or changes frequently.

ease.reason: A beginner can test draft wording on fictional order rows, but the source gives no data connection or delivery capability.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small online shops may pay for clearer status updates; this discussion establishes no purchase or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can draft from operator-supplied sample fields, while real data mapping and changing-status rules remain unknown.

autonomy.reason: A proposed loop can draft messages, but staff must resolve missing facts and approve every customer communication.

evidence.reason: The post explicitly asks about customer-facing status updates with incomplete or changing data, but gives no frequency or detailed rules.

candidates.reason: The concrete chore was assessed, but it repeats the ecommerce customer and customer-status communication workflow of prior post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6.

candidates.title: Capture and qualify incoming leads

demandEvidence.chore: Capture incoming leads and qualify them for follow-up.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I built a lead capture and qualification workflow in n8n using Apollo, OpenAI, Airtable, Slack, and Gmail.

ease.reason: A student could mock lead summaries from fictional records, but the source is a maker report and supplies no reusable implementation proof.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a professional service firm might pay for lead handling; this build report does not establish unmet demand or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic-data mock is possible, but useful qualification criteria and permissioned real lead inputs are not supplied.

autonomy.reason: A draft summary could be prepared repeatedly, but a person must define qualification rules and approve outreach; the source does not support this service.

evidence.reason: The maker says they built a lead-capture and qualification workflow; this establishes a build report, not an external request or recurring unmet chore.

candidates.reason: The concrete workflow was assessed, but the assigned post reports its author's build rather than an external unmet need; the supported demand and implementation evidence are insufficient.
